summary: Specifies TLS cipher suites that use a pre-shared key to authenticate an ephemeral elliptic curve Diffie-Hellman exchange. They provide perfect forward secrecy, so recorded traffic stays safe even if keys are exposed later. It extends RFC 4279, RFC 4492 and RFC 4785.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 5489 adds TLS cipher suites that use a pre-shared key to authenticate a fresh elliptic-curve key exchange. The exchange provides Perfect Forward Secrecy, while three suites provide no encryption.

subtitle: TLS cipher suites that combine a pre-shared key with ephemeral elliptic-curve key exchange

tldr.problem: The existing TLS pre-shared-key suites did not combine PSK authentication with ephemeral elliptic-curve Diffie-Hellman key exchange.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 5489 defines ECDHE_PSK suites that combine a pre-shared key with an ephemeral elliptic-curve exchange and specify how to form the premaster secret.
tldr.outcome: The suites provide Perfect Forward Secrecy. Three suites use NULL encryption and therefore do not provide confidentiality.

facts.label: Key exchange
facts.value: ECDHE authenticated with a pre-shared key

today: RFC 5489 is an Informational TLS cipher-suite document published in March 2009. The supplied metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: What ECDHE_PSK Adds
sections.content:
RFC 4279 defines TLS cipher suites that use pre-shared keys, RFC 4492 defines elliptic-curve key exchange, and RFC 4785 defines suites with authentication but no encryption. RFC 5489 combines a pre-shared key with an ephemeral elliptic-curve Diffie-Hellman exchange.

The resulting suites provide Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS): later exposure of the pre-shared key does not by itself reveal earlier session keys. The RFC expects readers to know the three earlier specifications.
sections.plainLanguage: These suites use a shared secret to authenticate a fresh key exchange. The fresh exchange helps protect earlier session keys if the shared secret is later exposed.

sections.title: The ECDHE_PSK Key Exchange
sections.content:
The client and server use the elliptic-curve parameter negotiation from RFC 4492. Their ServerKeyExchange and ClientKeyExchange messages carry the elliptic-curve parameters and the PSK identity information defined by RFC 4279.

To form the premaster secret, the endpoints concatenate the length of the ECDH result, the result itself, the length of the pre-shared key, and the key. The RFC requires the ServerKeyExchange message even if the server sends no PSK identity hint.
sections.plainLanguage: The endpoints exchange fresh elliptic-curve values and identify the pre-shared key they will use. They combine the key-exchange result and that shared key to form the premaster secret.

sections.title: The Cipher Suite Choices
sections.content:
The RFC defines four suites using SHA-1, two using SHA-2 hashes with AES, and three using NULL encryption. The encrypted suites specify RC4, 3DES, or AES with the corresponding message-authentication and pseudo-random functions.

The NULL-encryption suites provide authentication and integrity but do not hide data. The assigned suite values run from 0xC0,0x33 through 0xC0,0x3B.
sections.plainLanguage: Nine suites are defined. Six include encryption, while three only check who sent the data and whether it changed.

sections.title: Security and Registration
sections.content:
RFC 5489 says the security considerations of the referenced TLS and PSK specifications also apply. Because NULL-encryption suites provide no confidentiality, they should not carry sensitive information such as passwords.

The RFC assigns the nine cipher-suite values in the TLS Cipher Suite registry. It also advises implementers and administrators to follow published guidance on the strength of cryptographic algorithms.
sections.plainLanguage: Do not send passwords or other secrets using a NULL-encryption suite. The document also asks implementers to follow current guidance about cryptographic algorithms.
